Treatment summary
Patient presented following a side-impact collision at an intersection, reporting
headache, dizziness, and difficulty concentrating. The mechanism of injury is
consistent with the reported symptoms and with a concussion. Over nine visits, care
included symptom monitoring, cognitive and vestibular assessment, and graduated
actiivty guidance. The course of recovery was somewhat lnoger than typically expected
for this type of injury, and progress was gradual rather than linear. Examination
findings, including baalnce testing and reported symptom scores, support the diagnosis
of concussion, while certain neurological screening tests returned normal results. No
prior injury to the head or neck region is known from the patient history. Billing
records for two similar services on the same date are under review, and this summary
does not address those charges. Current assessment indicates ongoing improvement, with
return to full activity anticipated as symptoms continue to resolve.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.

- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
